paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: : Loss Ratio FLOPs
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the Loss Ratio (%) as a function of computational cost measured in TFLOPs (Tera Floating Point Operations per second), comparing different variants of the SepLLM model against a baseline "Vanilla" model. The x-axis is logarithmic, ranging from 1e7 to 9e8 TFLOPs, with tick marks at regular logarithmic intervals (1e7, 2e7, 5e7, 1e8, 2e8, 3e8, 4e8, 5e8, 6e8, 7e8, 8e8, 9e8). The y-axis is linear, ranging from 94% to 100% in increments of 1%, labeled as "Loss Ratio (%)". Five lines are plotted: the purple line with triangle markers represents the "Vanilla" model, which remains nearly constant at approximately 99.9% across all TFLOPs. The orange line with circle markers (SepLLM, n=64) starts at about 98.5% at 1e7 TFLOPs and increases to around 99.9% at 4e8 TFLOPs, then slightly declines. The blue line with x-markers (SepLLM, n=128) begins at 97% at 1e7 TFLOPs and rises to about 99.8% at 5e8 TFLOPs. The green line with diamond markers (SepLLM, n=64, H) starts at 97.2% at 1e7 TFLOPs, increases to approximately 99.9% at 3e8 TFLOPs, and remains stable. The red line with circle markers (SepLLM, n=64, H/T) starts at 94% at 1e7 TFLOPs, rises to about 98.8% at 5e8 TFLOPs, and then slightly decreases. All lines show an increasing trend in loss ratio with higher computational cost, with the red line being the lowest throughout the range.
